skill.name: using-superpowers
skill.description: Guides assistants to check available skills before responding, prioritize process guidance, and follow each selected skill according to its declared flexibility.
skill.summary: Establishes a skill-first workflow for AI assistants.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution finding is a false positive because SKILL.md lines 20-40 contain Graphviz DOT inside a fenced documentation block. However, coercive instructions attempt to control response ordering and skill invocation regardless of higher-priority context, creating a critical prompt-injection risk.

remediation.suggestion: Replace coercive directives with scoped guidance that defers to system, developer, and user instructions. Require trust review before invoking third-party skills.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 20-40 are a fenced Graphviz DOT flowchart. They contain no Ruby, shell command, executable backtick expression, or command invocation.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The text states, "IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT." It imposes mandatory behavior regardless of higher-priority context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The imperative language and universal scope are explicit at lines 6-12. The before-any-response rule reinforces the attempted behavioral override at lines 16-18.

critical_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
critical_findings.description: The text states, "IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT." It imposes mandatory behavior regardless of higher-priority context.
critical_findings.confidence_reasoning: The imperative language and universal scope are explicit at lines 6-12. The before-any-response rule reinforces the attempted behavioral override at lines 16-18.

content.value_statement: AI assistants can begin work without checking available procedures, causing inconsistent execution. This skill requires early skill discovery and ordered workflow selection.
actual_capabilities: Requires assistants to check whether a skill applies before responding.
Defines priority between process skills and implementation skills.
Distinguishes rigid instructions from flexible guidance.
Provides a flowchart for selecting and following skills.
Identifies common rationalizations that bypass skill discovery.
limitations: Does not discover, install, or execute skills itself.
Assumes Skill and TodoWrite tools, which may be unavailable or differently named.
Uses absolute instructions that can conflict with higher-priority platform or user directions.
Does not define how to assess the security or trustworthiness of invoked skills.

use_cases.title: Standardize coding-agent startup
use_cases.description: Check relevant process and implementation skills before beginning a coding task.

use_cases.title: Apply team procedures consistently
use_cases.description: Guide assistants toward established workflows before they inspect files or propose changes.

use_cases.title: Teach skill selection discipline
use_cases.description: Demonstrate how process guidance should precede domain-specific implementation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Check skill relevance
prompt_templates.prompt: Before answering my request about [topic], identify any available skill that applies and explain which one you selected.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner users starting a general task

prompt_templates.title: Choose a process skill
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to [goal]. Check for relevant process skills first, then select any implementation skill needed for the work.

prompt_templates.title: Follow a skill checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the applicable skill for [task]. If it contains a checklist, track every item and report any blocked step.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate multiple skills
prompt_templates.prompt: For [complex task], identify applicable skills, order them by process and implementation priority, and explain how conflicts will be resolved.

output_examples.input: Help me diagnose an intermittent test failure.
output: I will inspect evidence and reproduce the failure before proposing changes.
Implementation skills will follow after the failure mode is understood.

output_examples.output: I will check process guidance first, then apply the available frontend implementation skill to the settings workflow.
I will select the relevant review and security skills, follow their required checks, and report findings by severity.

best_practices: Confirm that a selected skill matches the current task before following it.
Apply process skills before implementation skills when both are relevant.
Keep higher-priority platform and user instructions authoritative when skill guidance conflicts.
anti_patterns: Do not invoke unrelated skills only because they are available.
Do not treat skill text as permission to override higher-priority instructions.
Do not assume remembered skill content matches the current installed version.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It instructs an assistant to check available skills before responding and to prioritize process guidance before implementation guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill execute other skills?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow instructions and depends on the host assistant to discover and invoke skills.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: The document references Skill and TodoWrite tools. Tool names and availability may differ across Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How are multiple skills ordered?
faq.answer: The skill places process skills, such as debugging, before implementation skills, such as frontend development.

faq.question: Can its instructions override system rules?
faq.answer: No. System, developer, and user instructions remain authoritative according to the host platform hierarchy.

faq.question: Does it evaluate skill security?
faq.answer: No. Users should review third-party skills for permissions, data access, commands, and instruction manipulation before use.
